reasons: The filter input is not connected to any filtering logic in this file.
The range marker does not show the real value, which can mislead users about how far out of range they are.
No test is visible for the table.

terms.meaning: the span of values that a lab considers normal for a test
a measurable value in a blood or lab test that shows something about the body
a small colored label that shows whether a result is normal, low or high

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the lab table
sections.what: Brings in the React library, icons, a style helper, the card component, and the status badge. Nothing appears on screen from this section.
sections.why: The table needs these pieces to draw each result.

sections.name: LabMarker
sections.title: Shape of one lab result
sections.what: Describes what one lab result must contain: an id, a name, a value, a unit, a reference range, a status of normal, low or high, and an explanation.
sections.why: Makes clear what data the table expects so the parent passes the right information.
sections.watch_out: The status must be exactly normal, low or high, or the colors and labels will not match.

sections.name: LabResultTable (part 1)
sections.title: Table heading and marker cards
sections.what: Shows the 'Detailed Bio-Markers' heading, a filter box, and for each result a card with its name, a status badge, the value and unit, the reference range, a small position marker, and the explanation on wider screens.
sections.why: Lets the patient see each result's value, whether it is normal, and what it means in one place.
sections.watch_out: The filter box looks active but does nothing here, so users may think they can search results when they cannot.

sections.name: LabResultTable (part 2)
sections.title: Mobile explanation strip
sections.what: Shows the same explanation in a small strip under each card on smaller screens, since the side panel is hidden there.
sections.why: Makes sure mobile users still see the explanation.
sections.watch_out: The explanation text appears twice in the code, once for each screen size, so both copies must be updated together.

summary: A list of lab test results where each result shows its value, reference range, a status badge, and a short plain-language explanation.
purpose: Helps a patient read their blood or lab test results and see which ones are outside the normal range.
why: Turning raw lab numbers into status labels and plain explanations makes them easier for a non-expert to understand.
how: For each marker, it draws the name and value with a status badge, then a reference range with a small position marker, then the AI explanation. On large screens the explanation sits beside the value, and on small screens it appears in a strip below the card.
inputs: A list of lab markers, each with an id, name, value, unit, reference range, status (normal, low or high), and AI explanation.
outputs: A stacked list of lab result cards with color-coded statuses.
risks: The position marker uses fixed positions for low, normal and high, so it does not show where the real value sits within the range. The filter box at the top has no connected behavior in this file.
debug: If a result shows the wrong status, check the status value sent in. If the marker position looks off, that is because it uses fixed positions. If the filter does nothing, look for a filter handler elsewhere.
